draw.summary: Draws a shape in the world for a while - the way to see what a script is computing.
params: how long it stays, in ticks
a map: the geometry of that type plus the common ones: `player`, `color`, `fill`, `line`, `follow`, `snap`, `seethrough`, `dim`, `debug`
draw.returns: `num` — how many players got it as a real shape rather than as particles.
examples:
// a ghost block, to show where a piece will go
shape.draw('block', 100, {'pos' -> pos, 'block' -> 'chest[facing=north]'});

// an ore behind a wall
shape.draw('box', 200, {'from' -> [10, 12, 10], 'to' -> [11, 13, 11], 'seethrough' -> true});
draw.note: Whoever has Blossom on the client sees the real shape; whoever plays vanilla sees the same geometry approximated with particles. You do not have to know which is which. A name the shape does not have is an error with the right one suggested, not a silent default, and a colour hand-written in hexadecimal with the alpha at zero is invisible, which is the mistake people make most.

clear.summary: Forgets the shapes still waiting to be redrawn as particles.
clear.note: It does not remove the ones already sent to a client: those expire on their own when their duration runs out.

types.summary: The names of the shapes `draw` accepts.
types.returns: `list` — the names of the shape types, in the order `draw` documents them.
